statement: Let S be the set of all node values in root, defined recursively by values(Tree.Null) = empty and values(Tree.Node(v,l,r)) = {v} union values(l) union values(r). Let m = min S. The function returns a result r and: if {x in S | x > m} is empty, then r = -1; otherwise r = min {x in S | x > m}.
preconditions: root is a non-empty special binary tree: root != Tree.Null; every node of root has either zero or two children (a leaf is Node(v, Null, Null)); for every internal node n of root, n.val = min(n.left.val, n.right.val); every node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2^31 - 1; and root has at most 25 nodes.

statement: For every root satisfying the preconditions, the function returns some result r and does not fail: there is no panic, no out-of-bounds access, and no i64 overflow.
preconditions: root is a non-empty special binary tree: root != Tree.Null; every node of root has either zero or two children (a leaf is Node(v, Null, Null)); for every internal node n of root, n.val = min(n.left.val, n.right.val); every node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2^31 - 1; and root has at most 25 nodes.

statement: Let S be the set of all node values in root. The function returns a result r and r = -1 if and only if S has exactly one element (equivalently, every node of root has value root.val).
preconditions: root is a non-empty special binary tree: root != Tree.Null; every node of root has either zero or two children (a leaf is Node(v, Null, Null)); for every internal node n of root, n.val = min(n.left.val, n.right.val); every node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2^31 - 1; and root has at most 25 nodes.

statement: Let S be the set of all node values in root. Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, there exists a node n of root such that n.val = r (that is, r is in S).
preconditions: root is a non-empty special binary tree: root != Tree.Null; every node of root has either zero or two children (a leaf is Node(v, Null, Null)); for every internal node n of root, n.val = min(n.left.val, n.right.val); every node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2^31 - 1; and root has at most 25 nodes.

statement: Let S be the set of all node values in root, m = min S, and M = max S. Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, m < r <= M and 1 <= r <= 2^31 - 1.
preconditions: root is a non-empty special binary tree: root != Tree.Null; every node of root has either zero or two children (a leaf is Node(v, Null, Null)); for every internal node n of root, n.val = min(n.left.val, n.right.val); every node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2^31 - 1; and root has at most 25 nodes.

statement: Let S be the set of all node values in root and m = min S. Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, no value x in S satisfies m < x < r; equivalently, for every x in S, if x > m then x >= r.
preconditions: root is a non-empty special binary tree: root != Tree.Null; every node of root has either zero or two children (a leaf is Node(v, Null, Null)); for every internal node n of root, n.val = min(n.left.val, n.right.val); every node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2^31 - 1; and root has at most 25 nodes.

statement: Let S1 be the set of all node values in root1 and spec_2 the set of all node values in root2. If S1 = S2, then the function returns a result r1 for root1 and a result r2 for root2, and r1 = r2.
preconditions: root1 and root2 each satisfy: it is a non-empty special binary tree (the root is not Tree.Null; every node has either zero or two children; for every internal node n, n.val = min(n.left.val, n.right.val)); every node value is in [1, 2^31 - 1]; and it has at most 25 nodes.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, there exists an internal node n of root (a node whose two children are non-null) such that n.val = root.val, one child of n has value root.val, and the other child of n has value r.
preconditions: root is a non-empty special binary tree: root != Tree.Null; every node of root has either zero or two children (a leaf is Node(v, Null, Null)); for every internal node n of root, n.val = min(n.left.val, n.right.val); every node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2^31 - 1; and root has at most 25 nodes.

statement: Let S be the set of all node values in root, m = min S, and let C = { c | there exists an internal node n of root such that n.val = m, c is the value of one of n's two children, and c > m }. If C is empty, the function returns r = -1; otherwise it returns r = min C.
preconditions: root is a non-empty special binary tree: root != Tree.Null; every node of root has either zero or two children (a leaf is Node(v, Null, Null)); for every internal node n of root, n.val = min(n.left.val, n.right.val); every node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2^31 - 1; and root has at most 25 nodes.
